newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to liquidate 57 banks, revoke licences.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to liquidate 57 banks, revoke licences.

text.p: Indonesia will liquidate at least 57 banks and revoke the licences of 50 others this year because of mismanagement, Bisnis Indonesia reported on Wednesday.

The paper quoted Nader Thaher, president-director of Balai Lelang Nusantara, as saying on Tuesday the banks would be liquidated or have their licences revoked because of mismanagement and other reasons.

Officials of Lelang Nusantara, the only private company appointed by the government to appraise the health of financial institutions, were not available for comment. A Finance Ministry official declined comment.
Nader was quoted as saying the banks had also failed to heed calls by monetary authorities for troubled banks to merge or be acquired in order to improve their performance.
"The 107 banks have asked PT Balai Lelang Nusantara to handle their problems. Most of them are banks which offer credit to the public," the paper said but gave no other details.
Nader said the liquidation was in line with the government's new regulations was aimed at improving protection for depositors.

The regulation, signed into effect by President Suharto on December 3, states that depositors will be given priority in the event of a bank's liquidation after the clearing employees' wages, auction fees, tax and administrative fees.

Nader said the central bank had decided to impose a reserve requirement of five percent and capital adequacy ratio (CAR) of eight percent from April this year. Paid-up capital was set at 50 billion rupiah for foreign exchange banks.
Central Bank director Heru Soepraptomo said last month the government had revoked the licences and liquidated more than 50 small and large banks since the country's independence in 1945.
